cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend, because we're hitting the road with Jesus and His disciples. The day of His ascension is getting close. And Jesus sets out with His mind made up.

cards.question: As the day of His ascension approaches, Jesus resolutely sets out for ___.

cards.text: Jesus sends messengers on ahead into a village of the Samaritans to make arrangements for Him. That's an advance team, friend, while the rest of us just pull into the driveway and text "outside" like that's a whole PLAN.

cards.question: Jesus' messengers reach the Samaritan village. How do the people there respond to Him?
Why does the Samaritan village refuse to welcome Jesus?

answers.text: They had never heard of Him

cards.text: James and John, two of Jesus' disciples, see all this. And they come to Jesus with an offer that is, uh… a LOT.

cards.question: James and John ask Jesus if He wants them to call down ___ from heaven to consume the people of that Samaritan village.
James and John offer to call down fire from heaven on the Samaritan village. What does Jesus do?

answers.text: He tells them to go ahead
He calls the fire down Himself

cards.text: So Jesus and His disciples just go on to another village. A whole village turns Him away and He keeps walking, while one cookie sticks to MY tray and I need to sit down a minute.
As they're walking along the road, someone says to Jesus, “I will follow You wherever You go.” WHEREVER. That is a big word, friend.

cards.question: Jesus answers the man who says he'll follow Him wherever: “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.” What is Jesus warning him about?

answers.text: Following Him means no settled home
The road ahead has wild animals
The man needs a house first

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to another man. This time, Jesus is the one doing the inviting.

cards.question: On the road, Jesus turns to another man. What does Jesus say to him?

cards.text: The man replies, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.” But Jesus tells him, “Let the dead bury their own dead.”

cards.question: Instead of burying his father first, what does Jesus tell this man to go do?

cards.text: Then still another man speaks up: “I will follow You, Lord; but first…” There's that word AGAIN.

cards.question: True or false: This third man asks Jesus to let him first say farewell to his family.

cards.text: Jesus answers him with a picture from the field: a man who puts his hand to the plow.

cards.question: In Jesus' picture, what does the man at the plow do that makes him not fit for the kingdom of God?

cards.text: Then Jesus declares, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.” Friend, I once stamped a whole tray while looking back over my shoulder at the oven, and I stamped the TABLE. Three times.

findings.problem: The setup line "This time, Jesus is the one doing the inviting" gives away card 13's answer. Of the three answers, only "Follow Me" is an invitation, so "Go home in peace" and "Wait here for Me" are ruled out before the baker reasons at all.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 20 repeats Luke 9:62 word for word, right after cards 18 and 19 already covered the plow, the looking back and "not fit for the kingdom of God." It adds nothing new from the passage, so it works as a recap of the answer the baker just gave. The joke could ride on card 18, or the plow picture could be told once.
Multiple choice dominates the stop: 7 of the 10 choice cards are multiple choice, with 2 fill in the blank and 1 true or false.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Card 14 is only the two BSB quotes, with no Papa Dorin voice and no storyteller line. The hard saying "Let the dead bury their own dead" lands with nothing around it.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
